main_text.l: للللرجال مكرمة للنسا Circumcisio
[necessarius] in fœminis honorabilis: cui addi potest
quod ab eodem refert Ebnol Athir, في الوليمة
الاعذار حق Æquum est ut circumcisiones convivio
celebrentur. Quod ad ipsum Mohammedem, eum na-
tum asserunt معذورا مسرورا Umbilico, & præputio,
præcisis. quod si fictum, ideò factum videtur,ut Mosi,
vel alicui alii è Patriarchis, de quibus idem asserunt
Iudæi, similis haberetur; sin verum, non adeò in-
solens fuisse, ut pueri recutiti nascerentur,apud gentes
circumcisionis observantes, patet ex iis quæ sta-
tuunt Iudæi in suis ad legem [illegible, ~10 letters] de iis, qui
hoc modo ex utero materno prodierint. Nisi forsan
verpum hunc sub Lunæ radiis natum putemus.
Credebant siquidem Arabes ان من ولد في القمر

l.i: Luna radiis nascerētur contrahi perinde ac circumcisio

Sanguis ] Videntur tamen Arabes antiquiores san-

l.i: guinem inter esculenta habuisse, unde inter ea, quæ

main_text.l: iis olim in usu erant, numeratur التسويں seu intestina
sanguine ad escam farciendi mos, apud authorem

الامعاء ويلقو ذه في النار ثم يأكلونه Sanguinem intestinis

main_text.l: Cibum istum مسون[?] Atoswadd, ab اسود quod nigrum
denotat, appellabant, ut nostrates Black pudding.
Ira autem conficiebatur ان يوخذ الدمران فتعصر فيها
الناقة ويشن راسها وذشري ويوكل descri-
bente.

marginalia.note: Et v. AlZamachilh, & Bidawium. in c. 5. Alc. ubi probibetur sanguis.

page.notes: Marginal notes: left margin, top: "AlGazal. & v. Mogreb. in" with an Arabic word below; left margin, middle: "Ebnol Athir. ibid."; left margin, bottom: Hebrew "קטן שנולד" and "בשהוא[?]", the last word only partly legible. The Greek word after "ad legem" is too blurred to read and is marked illegible. The Arabic passages are copied as seen and may contain small errors; the Arabic in the first line is partly obscured. The printed text is set in the same paragraph throughout, with no paragraph break on this part of the page. The first line of the Latin in the margin and the Hebrew heading are uncertain. The Arabic lines are read only roughly, and the Arabic word after "libri" and the word "Atoswadd" are doubtful. The blot in the left-margin note after "sanguis" hides part of the word. The word "describente" is split across two lines in the print.
